subject: Evaluating replacement: CloudCore vendor comparison and tailored bundle
messages:

Date: 2028-07-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring a replacement for VendorX — can Redwood close the gap?

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking a minute. Short background: CloudCore is re-evaluating our inference stack — VendorX has been our provider for two years but were seeing escalating unit costs and inconsistent latency at peak. Procurement asked me to collect realistic replacement economics and operational impacts before the next exec review.

Key asks wed like Redwood to address:
- A comparable list price + committed discount for a 12–24 month ramp (starting ~100M tokens/month, hitting ~350M in 9 months).
- Migration credits, tooling assistance (model conversion, KV cache warming), and any onboarding SLA credits.
- Comparisons of packaging options: per-token hosted vs reserved Dedicated capacity (GPU pools) vs Private (VPC).
- Any explicit egress or logging costs, and how Redwood supports HIPAA/SOC2 evidence for an audit.

I attached our RFP and a rough migration estimate. Happy to schedule 30 minutes to walk through.

Best,
Lloyd
CloudCore — Head of Platform Strategy

Vanessa — draft pricing and rationale below. I focused on keeping the entry economics attractive while protecting unit economics during the ramp. Notes inline.

Proposal (high level) — 12-month and 24-month options
A) 12-month "Rapid Onramp" (target: 100M -> 350M tokens/month in 9 months)
- Hosted API: base list price $0.00018/token -> committed tiered discount to reach $0.00012/token at 300M+ tokens/month. Average first-year blended $0.00014/token.
- Migration credit: $120k one-time (applied as invoice credit over first 3 months) for model conversion, KV cache warming, and pre-warm capacity.
- Pilot: 2-week pilot with $30k token credits to validate tail latencies.
- SLA onboarding credit: 10% refund on first monthly invoice if onboarding latency/availability SLO missed.

B) 24-month "Steady Reserve" (adds reserved Dedicated capacity)
- Dedicated reserved pool: annual commit equivalent to sustained 250M tokens/mo; pricing: effective $0.00009/token (based on GPU pool commit + managed support).
- One-time migration credit: $200k and two weeks of funded engineering time to integrate runtime optimizations (KV prefetch, quantization tuning).
- Early termination: pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity after 6 months minus migration credit recoupment schedule (standard 6-12 month clawback).

Operational & cost caveats (Marcus please review):
- Egress/logging: include a capped logging ingestion fee: $0.01/GB after 100GB/day. Recommend including the first 2TB/month free for the first 3 months.
- Private/VPC: add 6–8 week lead time for on-prem or VPC private deployments plus a one-time infra setup fee ($75k) for catalogue, KMS integration, and audit evidence export.

Commercial levers to offer vs VendorX:
- Migration credit + pilot credits (differentiator).
- Short-term blended discount target to beat VendorX list by ~12–20% in year one.
- Packaging: allow a path to migrate from Hosted -> Dedicated with price protection for 3 months after conversion.

Attachments to outbound: price-sheet (CSV) + migration timeline (pptx) + compliance checklist.

If we agree on these numbers I can produce a compact outbound email and a one-page comparison vs VendorX for Lloyd's exec deck.

— Jordan
Principal Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposal: migration path, pilot, and two pricing options (summary)

Hi Lloyd — thanks again for the RFP. Attached is a concise summary and a one-page comparison vs VendorX (high level). Below are the options we recommend to match your objectives.

TL;DR — two recommended commercial paths
1) Rapid Onramp (12-month) — minimal upfront infra, fast pilot, $120k migration credit, expected blended first-year unit cost ~ $0.00014/token. Pilot credits $30k, 2-week validation.
2) Steady Reserve (24-month) — reserved Dedicated capacity, larger migration credit $200k + two weeks funded eng, effective $0.00009/token at steady state. Includes path-to-private option with 6–8 week lead time and one-time infra fee.

Operational notes:
- Well include the first 2TB/month of logging/ingest free for 90 days. After that out-of-scope logging is billed as discussed.
- Well provide SOC2 attestation and a compliance packet (exportable logs + KMS integration notes); Private deployments include additional evidence exports.

Next steps:
- If either option looks like the right starting point, can we schedule a 45-minute exec+procurement sync this week? Janet from procurement (copied) suggested Friday morning PT.
- Well follow with the full price-sheet and a one-page comparison for your exec pack.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
